summary: Sargramostim is a recombinant human granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) that stimulates proliferation and differentiation of myeloid progenitor cells. It shortens time to neutrophil recovery and reduces severe infection after AML induction chemotherapy, mobilizes peripheral blood progenitor cells, accelerates myeloid reconstitution after bone marrow or stem cell transplant, and is used for hematopoietic syndrome of acute radiation exposure. It is given IV or subcutaneously with twice-weekly CBC monitoring.
indications: Shorten neutrophil recovery and reduce infection after induction chemotherapy in adults 55 years and older with acute myeloid leukemia (AML)
Mobilization of hematopoietic progenitor cells into peripheral blood for leukapheresis and autologous transplantation
Acceleration of myeloid reconstitution after autologous or allogeneic bone marrow / peripheral blood progenitor cell transplantation
Treatment of delayed neutrophil recovery or graft failure after bone marrow transplantation
Increase survival in adult and pediatric patients acutely exposed to myelosuppressive doses of radiation (hematopoietic syndrome of acute radiation syndrome)

dosage.n: Start ~day 11 or 4 days after chemo; continue until ANC >1500/mm3 x3 days

dosage.d: 250 mcg/m2/day IV over 24 h or subcutaneously once daily

dosage.c: After peripheral blood progenitor cell transplant
dosage.d: 250 mcg/m2/day IV over 24 h or subcutaneously once daily
dosage.n: Begin immediately after infusion of progenitor cells
Start 2-4 h after bone marrow infusion, >=24 h after last chemo/radiation

dosage.d: 250 mcg/m2/day IV over 2 hours for 14 days
dosage.n: May repeat course after 7-day rest if engraftment not achieved

dosage.d: Weight-based subcutaneous dose once daily (e.g., 7 mcg/kg in adults)
dosage.n: Start as soon as feasible after suspected/confirmed exposure

admin: Administer by IV infusion or subcutaneous injection per indication
Reconstitute lyophilized powder; if used in pregnancy or neonates use preservative-free Sterile Water for Injection (benzyl alcohol risk)
Do not administer within 24 hours of chemotherapy or 12 hours of radiotherapy
Discontinue if blast cells appear or disease progression occurs
moa: Sargramostim is recombinant GM-CSF, a colony-stimulating factor that binds specific cell-surface receptors to support survival, clonal expansion, and differentiation of hematopoietic progenitor cells along the granulocyte-macrophage pathway (neutrophils, monocytes/macrophages, dendritic cells). It also activates mature granulocytes and macrophages and can promote megakaryocyte and erythroid progenitor proliferation.

absolute: History of serious allergic reaction including anaphylaxis to GM-CSF/sargramostim, yeast-derived products, or any component
Use within 24 hours of chemotherapy or 12 hours of radiotherapy
relative: Excessive leukemic myeloid blasts in marrow or peripheral blood (>=10%)
monitor: Respiratory status and oxygenation during infusion

preg: Limited human data; based on animal studies may cause embryofetal harm. Use only if clearly needed. If used in pregnancy, reconstitute only with preservative-free Sterile Water for Injection because benzyl alcohol can cause gasping syndrome in neonates.
lact: It is not known whether sargramostim is excreted in human milk. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and any potential adverse effects on the infant.
renal: No specific dose adjustment provided. Monitor renal function periodically; reduce or interrupt dosing if renal dysfunction develops, particularly in patients with pre-existing impairment.
hepatic: Monitor liver function. Elevations in bilirubin and hepatic enzymes can occur, especially with pre-existing hepatic impairment; reduce dose or interrupt therapy if levels rise.

moderate: Myelosuppressive chemotherapy and radiotherapy (do not co-administer within the specified windows; may blunt effect or increase blast proliferation)
Corticosteroids and lithium (may potentiate myeloproliferative effect)
minor: Drugs causing fluid retention may worsen edema/effusions
interactions.diagnostics: May transiently raise WBC, and increase liver enzymes, bilirubin, and creatinine

serious: First-dose reaction (flushing, hypotension, tachycardia, dyspnea, hypoxia)
Capillary leak / fluid retention with pleural and pericardial effusions
emergency: Symptomatic pleural or pericardial effusion / cardiac compromise

monitoring: CBC with differential twice weekly (watch for excessive blast or WBC counts)
Renal and hepatic function in patients with pre-existing impairment
Respiratory symptoms and oxygen saturation during/after infusion
Fluid status, body weight, signs of effusion
Vital signs with the first dose for infusion reactions
counsel: This medicine is given by injection or infusion under medical supervision
Bone pain and flu-like symptoms are common and usually manageable
Report difficulty breathing, swelling, palpitations, or rash promptly
Frequent blood tests are needed to monitor your white-cell count
Tell your team about any heart, lung, or kidney problems
pk: WBC rise typically begins within days of starting therapy
Subcutaneous peak concentration around 1-3 hours; IV peak immediately post-infusion
Once-daily dosing; effect maintained over the treatment course
Refrigerate at 2-8 C; do not freeze or shake; protect from light
pearls: GM-CSF acts on a broader range of myeloid cells than G-CSF (filgrastim), including macrophages and dendritic cells
Watch for a first-dose reaction with hypotension and hypoxia
Hold around chemotherapy/radiotherapy by the specified time windows
Reconstitute with preservative-free diluent for neonates and pregnancy (benzyl alcohol gasping syndrome)
missed: Doses are given by a healthcare provider on a set schedule; if a scheduled dose is missed, contact the treatment team for guidance rather than self-administering an extra dose.
overdose: Doses up to 16 times the recommended dose produced WBC rises up to 200,000/mm3 with reversible dyspnea, malaise, nausea, fever, rash, tachycardia, headache, and chills. In overdose, discontinue therapy and monitor WBC count and respiratory status; effects resolve after stopping the drug.
